Really great game. Gameplay being so simple yet so addictive (and hard at times). The game design being really good and level layouts not really going to piss you off (unlike the second game). Most mistakes are by you, or your luck running out.
Also has an interesting story, somehow really deep despite how simple the game seems.
Would recommend for an 3-5 hour game (if you're going for all the achievements) with deep story and addictive gameplay.

Hotline Miami is a fast-paced run-and-gun shooter focused on fast thinking and decision taking.
The storyline (mostly) revolves around a guy called Jacket who receives strange phonecalls from a mysterious organisation giving you an adress and a series of analogies about taking everyone on this adress out. You are given an animal-themed mask to execute the killings with. Each mask unlocked gives you a new abillity.
The missions are played with a smooth electronic 80's inspired soundtrack playing in the background, projecting a sense of the drug-crimes of 1980s Miami
The mindless killing is numbed out by the 8-bit pixely graphics of the game, giving the game a strange feeling of discomfort and absurdity to it.
Minor cons with the games is the limited storyline that (only) takes around 2-4 hours to complete.

Overall I would rate the game a strong 8 out of 10 for great gameplay, soundtrack, and graphics, but mildly lacking replayabillity.

This game is infuriating, but quite obviously. This game is intended to provide a challenge (as of writing this it's part of Perfect Random's Difficult Games Bash sale) which is probably why I still enjoy this game even after the CBT-tier levels the late game throws at you.

The story (in this game, at least. HM2 does seem to build upon it) is quite lacking, but that isn't really the reason people came here. The graphics too are quite ugly in places (mainly the dialogue sprite faces) but in a similar fashion to Cruelty Squad, it adds more charm to the game's experience. The levels are designed quite well and you can pull off some quite satisying stunts if you spend enough time with this game (I haven't) as well as a vibe that at the time was quite untapped in games.

Overall, I do recommend this game. It is fairly short if you are going for a straight shot through the story, and it is fun yet also torturous to go through and 100%. At any price point it is worth the money, however if you are a stickler for low prices and sales (like me) it does frequently go on sale throughout the year at an even lower price.

Hotline Miami is both an amazingly engaging and fun game as well as one with the potential to frustrate one to the point of submission.

The psychedelic aesthetic and late 80's coke-binged atmosphere are amazing, punctuated further by a pulsing, trippy, and sleepy Sunday morning style soundtrack that will assault the ears with thick bass and beats as much as it will soothe them with drugged-out experimental compositions.

The fast and frantic nature of the gameplay is satisfying and visceral, and it's hard not to get just a little giddy while you paint the floors and walls with your enemies' remains. There's so much moment to moment fun in Hotline Miami that it's easy to recommend on that alone.

Drawbacks however come from the lack of precision with controls and difficulty spikes that are entirely and at times pretty unfair. Aiming melee and ranged weapons alike is quite an ordeal with keyboard+mouse or a gamepad and that lack of precision will cause a lot of unwarranted deaths. Enemy AI is at times completely random in its behaviour and what amounts to boss battles in the game are really the worst parts of the game.

If left in the oven just a bit longer to work out the control and AI issues, Hotline Miami would have been one for the ages. As it stands, it's easy to recommend with the only caveat being a patience for failure that may sometimes not be your fault.

Probably one of the best indie game of 2012.
The game mechanics are simple but effective, you enter a room with a simple goal of killing every single person in it the goriest way possible.
You have lots of weapons, guns, knives and stuff to throw at your enemies.
Your character is controlled from the top like the first GTA.
The graphics are really great with that old school tone of Pink.
Several Masks are available that grant you passive skills and give your a certain style before slaughtering everybody.
But the best think in my opinion that makes the game truly awesome is the Soundtrack.
Probably one of the best OST out there that turns every kill you make in the game a moment of pure joy.
All of that combine make Hotline Miami a must have from the indie scene.
Not to mention that you can replay the game to obtain the highest score and unlock all the remaining masks.

Hotline Miami is good.
Some people say its too hard. Well, that's the point. I mean, there's legitimately an achievement for doing 1,000 times.

It's all about rinse and repeat, learning the map layout, enemy placement, enemy types, and mask abilities and how to use them to your advantage.

A game that came out relatively recently, Deathloop, shares this "rinse and repeat" pattern with Hotline Miami, and as a result shares a lot of the player behaviour exhibited in Hotline Miami, learning the layout, placement, types, abilities, and how to use them creatively.

The story has a shocking amount of depth for such simple graphics and gameplay. The whole thing just works. I just beat the game, including the epilogue and bonus levels, and I already want more.
